reden: No. The report’s findings cover: (1) liquidator reward unit mismatch in executeLiquidate (different-decimal tokens), (2) borrow aToken cap bypass via multicall end-check using balanceOf instead of totalSupply, (3) unconditional oracle call in collateralRatio for zero-debt users, and (4) missing 18-decimal normalization for collateral. The described vulnerability is a race/authorization logic issue between executeRepay and executeLiquidateWithReplacement where repay only checks debtPositionId and not the borrower, enabling a user’s repay to settle a different borrower’s debt after replacement. Different vulnerability type (race/authorization vs unit/logic/cap/oracle/decimals), different code path (repay + liquidateWithReplacement vs executeLiquidate), and different fix (add borrower check to repay vs unit conversion). Fixing any reported issues would not fix the repay/race problem.
